senses.sense_definition: To skim, leaf through, or flick rapidly through pages, papers, or similar flat items.

examples.text: She began to <w>riffle</w> through the stack of letters on her desk.
He stopped to <w>riffle</w> through the notebook in search of her address.

senses.sense_definition: To shuffle playing cards by splitting the deck and flicking the edges together with the thumbs.

examples.text: The dealer began to <w>riffle</w> the cards with practiced ease.
You should <w>riffle</w> the deck several times before dealing a hand.

senses.sense_definition: To ruffle or cause to flutter with a rippling movement, such as by a breeze.

examples.text: A cool evening breeze began to <w>riffle</w> the surface of the calm lake.
The wind continued to <w>riffle</w> the loose papers sitting on the porch.

senses.sense_definition: To idly manipulate or fiddle with small objects using one's fingers.

examples.text: He nervously began to <w>riffle</w> the coins in his coat pocket.
She sat listening intently, continuing to <w>riffle</w> through the pens on the table.

senses.sense_definition: To flow swiftly and shallowly over rocks or an uneven bed, producing small ripples.

examples.text: Clear mountain water seemed to <w>riffle</w> across the smooth stones below.
We watched the stream <w>riffle</w> gently past the grassy bank.

senses.sense_definition: To divide or sample material mechanically using a riffler.

examples.text: The laboratory technician had to <w>riffle</w> the crushed ore before running the test.
Geologists often <w>riffle</w> soil samples to obtain representative portions.

senses.sense_definition: A quick skim or flick through the pages of a book or papers.

examples.text: A quick <w>riffle</w> through the textbook revealed several missing diagrams.
With a careless <w>riffle</w> of the documents, she handed them back to him.

senses.sense_definition: A shuffle of playing cards performed by letting the edges of two halves interlace.

examples.text: He mixed the deck smoothly with an impressive <w>riffle</w>.
The dealer gave the cards a quick <w>riffle</w> before the next round.

senses.sense_definition: A shallow, fast-flowing section of a stream or river where the surface is broken into small ripples.

examples.text: They waded into the rocky <w>riffle</w> where trout often fed on insects.
The stream widened into a shallow <w>riffle</w> before entering the quiet pool.

senses.sense_definition: A small wave, ripple, or succession of tiny ripples on the surface of water.

examples.text: A sudden breeze stirred a gentle <w>riffle</w> across the pond.
The calm lake showed barely a <w>riffle</w> under the morning sky.

senses.sense_definition: The rapid fluttering sound produced when cards or pages are rapidly flipped.

examples.text: She heard the familiar <w>riffle</w> of cards from the back room.
The distinct <w>riffle</w> echoed as he let the pages snap back.

senses.sense_definition: A cleat, groove, or stepped trough used in mining to catch gold particles when washing gravel.

examples.text: Gold flakes settled behind each <w>riffle</w> along the bottom of the sluice.
He scraped the collected sediment carefully from the wooden <w>riffle</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A small metal disc attached to the end of a tool used in seal engraving.

examples.text: The artisan polished the delicate design using a fine <w>riffle</w>.
A worn <w>riffle</w> was replaced to maintain the precision of the engraving.
Professor <w>Riffle</w> delivered an inspiring lecture on environmental science.
Several members of the <w>Riffle</w> family attended the annual reunion.
